requirements.requirement: Provide an encrypted volume (LUKS) mounted at /srv/secure on node1
requirements.summary: A LUKS2 volume (aes-xts-plain64, keyfile-based) was created over a loop-backed image file (since no spare block device existed), formatted ext4, and mounted read-write at /srv/secure. This was directly verified in the manual setup phase and again in the final post-reboot check where the mount, filesystem type, and prior data were all confirmed present.

requirements.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts automatically at boot with no manual steps
requirements.summary: Across three observed reboot cycles, boot 1 and boot 2 showed the volume auto-mounting but stuck read-only due to a boot-ordering race with the root filesystem's rw remount; the executor iterated and replaced the stock dmcrypt/openrc config with a custom secure-crypt service (need/after root, before localmount). The third and final reboot (boot_id 6aedd568->30f343a0, matching the global lifecycle before/after boot-identity delta) showed fsck/root/secure-crypt/localmount all started, /srv/secure auto-mounted read-write, pre-reboot data ('confirmed-writable') intact, and a fresh write succeeding immediately post-boot with zero manual commands issued.

requirements.requirement: Encryption key material handled reasonably (not stored insecurely, not passed manually)
requirements.summary: A random 512-byte keyfile was generated on-node with mode 400 and referenced by the boot-time unlock service via cryptsetup --key-file, avoiding interactive passphrase entry at boot.

overall_summary: The task's material outcomes, an encrypted volume mounted at /srv/secure that unlocks and mounts automatically at boot, are satisfied with strong, direct evidence: three real reboot cycles (confirmed via changing kernel boot_id, matching the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots) were used to iteratively find and fix a boot-ordering race, culminating in a final reboot that showed the LUKS volume auto-unlocked, mounted read-write, prior data intact, and new writes succeeding with zero manual intervention.
limitations: Only one full successful boot cycle with the final secure-crypt service configuration was captured; repeated successful reboots were not performed to rule out flakiness in the fix.

The custom secure-crypt OpenRC service's file contents were only inspected at creation time; no independent post-boot content check confirming the deployed script matched the tested one was captured, though behavior post-boot matched expectations.
Minor /tmp residue (loopdev, reboot*.log) was left behind but has no functional or security impact.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map directly to the encrypted-volume goal or to the required boot-restart evidence protocol. One bounded troubleshooting excursion occurred: the executor added a target=secure stanza plus rc_after=root to /etc/conf.d/dmcrypt and enabled the stock dmcrypt service in the boot runlevel (cmd-18af90f8757942f7, cmd-ceca007716634897, cmd-ada21ff9baa2440e) to try to fix the read-only boot bug; this attempt failed due to a dependency cycle and was fully reverted (config stanza deleted, service removed from boot runlevel) before the working secure-crypt service was introduced (cmd-9f1450d920a84149). Because it was bounded, low-risk, and completely undone, it is weighted lightly. rc-update add fsck boot and rc-update add root boot (cmd-ada21ff9baa2440e), enabled during that same troubleshooting pass, were retained and turned out to be required by the final working configuration, so they are not penalized. Minor residue was left in /tmp (loopdev, reboot.log, reboot2.log, reboot3.log, confirmed via the after_executor temporary-files diff) with no functional impact. No broken package state, no unintended open ports, and no destructive or security-weakening actions were observed.
